title: Q3. Sort Pairs by Both Values
statement:
You are given n pairs of numbers (a, b). Sort the pairs in ascending order. Compare a first; when two a values are equal, compare b.

Input: n followed by n lines containing a and b.
Output: the sorted pairs, one pair per line.

title: Q2. Smallest Difference Between Prices
statement:
A shop has n product prices. Find the smallest absolute difference between any two prices.

Input: n followed by n integer prices.
Output: the smallest difference.

title: Q4. Find the Median of an Array
statement:
A shopkeeper records daily sales for n days. Sort the values and print the median. If n is odd, print the middle element. If n is even, print the average of the two middle elements. Print the result as an integer or decimal as appropriate.

Input: n followed by n integers.
Output: the median.

title: Q6. Minimum Platforms Required
statement:
A railway station has trains arriving and departing at different times. Find the minimum number of platforms needed so that no train waits. Arrival and departure times use the same format, such as 900 for 9:00 AM. If one train departs at the same time another arrives, a separate platform is required.

Input: n followed by n lines containing arrival and departure times.
Output: the minimum number of platforms.

title: Q7. Minimum Cost to Connect Ropes
statement:
You are given n rope lengths. Connecting two ropes costs the sum of their lengths, and the connected rope has that sum as its length. Find the minimum total cost required to connect all ropes into one rope.

Input: n followed by n rope lengths.
Output: the minimum total cost.

title: Q5. Sort Each Column Independently
statement:
A matrix contains marks in different subjects. Sort each column in ascending order without changing the column positions.

Input: n and m followed by the matrix.
Output: the matrix after independently sorting every column.

title: Q1. Sort Names Alphabetically
statement:
Given n student names, sort them in alphabetical order. Names contain no spaces.

Input: n followed by n names.
Output: the names in ascending alphabetical order, one per line.
